schema.scalability: Completion-style access paths at 20k-100k synsets on SQLite/commodity hardware: (1) 'all bridges for topic t' / 'for vehicle v' / 'by proposer' — index-served (idx_metaphor_bridges_topic/_vehicle/_proposer); 'bridges through intermediate x' — idx_metaphor_bridge_steps_via; 'verdict for bridge' — UNIQUE(bridge_id,judged_by) auto-index; 'all live edges' — idx_metaphor_judgments_label. All O(log n + k); even 100k-1M bridge rows are trivial. (2) graph_edges is a 4-arm UNION ALL view; SQLite pushes WHERE src_synset_id=? into each arm: has_property arm (822,807 rows) hits idx_spc_synset, dst-side hits property_vocab_curated UNIQUE(synset_id); metonym arm hits idx_synset_metonyms_synset; antonym arm's vocab_id_b side is unindexed but the table is 576 rows — no table-scan risk at current or 100k scale. Unfiltered full-view scans materialise ~900k rows — acceptable batch-wise, not per-request. The view emits duplicate multiplicity by design (documented at SCHEMA.sql:463-475); consumers must DISTINCT. (3) BLOB embeddings: synset_centroids = packed 300xfloat32 (~1.2KB) keyed by synset_id PK — point lookups cheap; the Go API preloads the ENTIRE table into RAM at startup (api/internal/db/cascade_cache.go:42-77, maps sized for 80k/40k) ≈ ~100MB at 81k rows, ~125-150MB at 100k — fits school-grade commodity hardware but is a fixed RAM floor; SQLite has no vector index, so any 'nearest vehicles to topic centroid' ranking is an O(N) in-app scan (~30M mults at 100k x 300-d ≈ tens of ms — fine per-query; all-pairs O(N^2) infeasible — candidate gating mandatory). Geometry features (max_hop_cos) are app-side per-path BLOB fetches (k PK lookups per bridge) — must be precomputed/persisted for training-scale use (the existing chain_geometry JSONL is exactly that workaround). (4) Cold-start/feature-provider queries: the cascade candidate CTE (api/internal/db/cascade.go:139-219, cluster-overlap join via idx_spc_cluster) is the measured envelope — ~350ms per broad lemma at 107k synsets WITH idx_lemmas_synset_id, 3-4s without (SCHEMA.sql:41-48), 16s variant rejected for correlated COUNT — i.e. index discipline, not engine choice, is the binding factor; SQLite is adequate. (5) Liabilities: no index on synset_properties.property_type (type-pivot queries scan 974k rows; access synset-first instead); centroid coverage is enrichment-bound (81,185 of 107,519 synsets — geometry features undefined off-cohort; the 20k-enrichment MVP goal and the held 10k run gate coverage); dead property_similarity adds ~1.5M rows of file bloat in both DBs; single-writer SQLite is fine for a single-operator grading loop.
schema.unit_of_representation: Strictly synset-keyed: topic_synset_id/vehicle_synset_id/via_synset_id all FK synsets(synset_id) (TEXT numeric strings, e.g. '72810'); all POS representable since synsets.pos covers n/v/a/r/s, so verbs/adjectives CAN be endpoints — but nothing marks POS on the edge itself (join required). Noun-primacy is baked into resolution, not schema: lookup_primary_synset (metaphor_graph.py:405-493) prefers curated-vocab noun senses by ascending polysemy, with lemmatised fallback (-s/-ing) for ~9% of vehicles arriving as plurals/gerunds; snap_concept_string (:306-357) resolves path concepts exact+morphological against property_vocab_curated (no embedding stage). The lemma SURFACE FORM actually graded is not stored anywhere on the edge — once snapped, 'smelting' vs 'smelt' vs which sense was chosen is unrecoverable; sense_attributes (sensekey PK, tagcount, idx_sense_attributes_lemma_tagcount) provides a dominant-sense prior (53% curated coverage, 91% unique-winner) but the bridge layer never records which sensekey/sense-choice produced its synset ids. Sense-splits are a live data problem, not hypothetical: 95 verdicts contain 19 distinct topic lemmas but 22 distinct topic_synset_ids — anger graded as synset 30227 (round 1) AND 72770 (round 2), argument as 70725 AND 67993 — so a synset-level completion model sees fragmented, disjoint supervision for what the operator experiences as one topic, on top of already-minimal synset-level edge recurrence (5/248). There is no alias/equivalence layer; the only recourse is joining through lemmas/sense_attributes at query time, which the schema permits but nothing canonicalises. Conversely path identity (path_hash = sha256 over ordered intermediate synset ids) means two surface-distinct but same-synset paths correctly collapse, while a bad_head mis-snap silently mints a different bridge identity — head-extraction errors (~31-35% of graded rows) therefore corrupt edge identity, not just labels.
schema.verdict: UNFIT AS-IS for the fitness definition, though the bridge-centric core (path-first proposals, multi-proposer pool, per-(bridge,judge) verdicts, idempotent hashing, FK-to-synset spine) is the right skeleton and its index shape comfortably supports completion-style queries at 20k-100k synsets on commodity hardware. It fails on three load-bearing counts: (a) it cannot losslessly store the verdicts it exists to learn from — the 95 graded JSONL records (two-axis v2 verdicts, tiers, tags incl. bad_head, ordinal confidence, rounds, supersedes chains) cannot be imported into the single-enum metaphor_judgments without destroying exactly the axes (linkage-vs-liveness, bad_head) that the verified analyses condition on; (b) it persists the four cascade features measured at chance for liveness while having no columns for the only verified signal (max_hop_cos/std_hop_cos path geometry, within-topic AUC 0.64-0.67, 0.85 bad_head-clean) nor the per-step phrase/head data needed to diagnose the 31-35% bad_head contamination; (c) it is universally unpopulated — 0 bridge rows in the one DB that has the DDL, no DDL at all on staging (contrary to working assumptions), truth living in worktree-pinned JSONL with no materialisation ever run — so 'metaphor-graph-completion' currently has no graph. TOP 3 SCHEMA CHANGES: (1) Verdict-model v2 alignment: replace/augment metaphor_judgments.label with linkage TEXT + metaphor TEXT axes, a judgment_tags child table (bad_head/leap/padding + tiers), ordinal confidence, round INTEGER, and versioned verdicts (drop UNIQUE(bridge_id,judged_by) in favour of (bridge,judge,judged_at) with a latest-view, preserving supersedes) — prerequisite for any lossless import of the existing 89-95 verdicts. (2) Persist the signal: add max_hop_cos/std_hop_cos/n_hops (nullable REAL) to metaphor_bridges and phrase TEXT + head TEXT + snap_method/snap_score to metaphor_bridge_steps, so geometry features are queryable/indexable and bad_head becomes a stored, auditable property rather than a JSONL tag. (3) Lemma/sense anchoring + actually materialise: add topic_lemma/vehicle_lemma (+ optional sensekey FKs into sense_attributes) to metaphor_bridges and a topic-alias resolution (same-lemma synset grouping) so cross-round sense-splits (19 lemmas -> 22 synset ids) aggregate instead of fragment; then run the planned JSONL->metaphor_bridges import against the typed main DB and apply the DDL to staging. Secondary cleanups that matter for the commodity-hardware envelope: drop the dead 1.55M-row property_similarity table from both DBs, and define the chain_signature<->path_hash bridge so 4,390 precomputed geometry rows can be reused rather than recomputed.

BATCH-COUPLED ID DISCIPLINE: batched prompts (enrichment, gap-fill, head extraction, disambiguation) key responses on the model echoing input IDs/lemmas/phrases exactly; mismatches are silently dropped (logged as unknown-ID warnings) or fall back (first-token heads), so per-item loss is invisible in aggregate outputs.

ALL PROMPTS ASSUME FRONTIER CLAUDE VIA CLI: no local/offline-LLM variants exist or have been calibrated, despite the school-deployment data-sovereignty constraint; generation costs (~$0.25/topic Haiku+Sonnet) and the persona judge's calibration are unquantified for self-hosted models.
prompts.fitness_assessment: The prompt suite captures the minimum a metaphor-graph-completion scorer needs — sense-vetted topic endpoints, candidate vehicles, ordered hop labels with single-word heads, and human verdicts keyed by chain_signature — but it systematically discards the three things extrapolation to NOVEL pairs would lean on: (1) trustworthy per-step synset identity (bad_head ~31% comes from asking for a bare head WORD and then snapping it with a least-polysemy heuristic the model never sees — the only verified geometric signal, max_hop_cos within-topic AUC 0.67, rises to 0.85 on the bad_head-clean subset, so this is the single largest measured signal leak); (2) edge typing/rationale (no prompt asks what KIND of conceptual move a hop is, or why it is apt — chains are untyped polylines in embedding space); (3) already-paid-for soft labels (Haiku vehicle confidence, proxy-judge confidence+reason are emitted and dropped). SINGLE HIGHEST-SIGNAL-PER-DOLLAR FORMAT CHANGE: extend the chain-generation output schema from {phrase, head} to {phrase, head, gloss} — a 3-8-word sense gloss per intermediate step (or, better when DB-wired, have the runner present the head's candidate synset glosses and ask the model to pick an index, reusing the existing gloss-match prompt pattern from metaphor_disambiguate.py:232-258). This costs a few dozen output tokens per chain (marginal against the $0.19/topic Sonnet spend), requires no new calls, collapses the bad_head layer at its source, makes every per-step synset_id verifiable, and retroactively protects both the path-geometry features and verdict transfer across regenerated chains. Second-best (cheap, additive): persist judge {verdict, confidence, reason} per sampled chain_signature to a JSONL — it is free weak supervision for the unbuilt live/dead judge that the context-free-edges refutation identified as the real bottleneck. For the school/self-hosted constraint, note that generation-time prompts are an offline build step (sovereignty-compatible); only the eventual scorer must run on commodity hardware, and nothing in these formats yet records what a small local model would need for distillation (rationales, confidences) — another reason to stop discarding them.

attempts.pattern: Three regularities dominate the history. (1) EVERY static-similarity substrate fails for cross-domain metaphor liveness, in every framing tried: pointwise property overlap in all reweightings (M02: all variants within ±0.06 of null), cosine bands (M04 v2: 0/negative sep), shared features/embeddings/WordNet relations/glosses/multi-hop traversal (context-free spike: AUC 0.50-0.55, mostly ANTI-correlated), and the cascade's own features against human labels (completion harness: raw scalar AUC≈0.50). The measured root cause is structural, not a tuning failure — the bridge feature of a live metaphor is contextually constructed (only 0.31% of LLM-claimed bridge features exist in both concepts' static enrichments), and cross-domain metaphor is by definition the low-surface-similarity case, so any similarity-encoding substrate selects synonyms (the inapt direction). (2) What works is (a) building the measurement instrument FIRST and validating it adversarially (M01 sensitivity, cohort-shape diagnostics, the 11-agent fact-check, the 5-auditor path-signal audit, the planned κ harness) — every instrument that was NOT measured against gold failed silently (Haiku extraction-evaluator blind to ~31% bad_head; the Forge Reader triage's ~1% bad_head estimate vs 31% reality); and (b) human-judged, contextually-generated artifacts: Haiku→Sonnet generation is ~71% live by Julian's grading and cheap ($0.20-0.29/topic), and the only genuinely new positive scoring signal in the whole programme — path-geometry max_hop_cos 0.64-0.67 within topic, 0.85 clean-subset — lives in the geometry of generated-then-graded chains, exactly the explicit-edge layer of the metaphor-graph-completion hypothesis. (3) The recurring failure mode is eval-cohort/objective misalignment: MUNCH is paraphrase-style (M04 v1 measured nothing), Phase 2 and Lakoff have inverted discriminator profiles so global knob-tuning is zero-sum (Karpathy loops; later noise audit showed several committed 'wins' were sub-1σ), Lakoff itself is a DEAD-metaphor cohort misaligned with the live-metaphor product goal, and proxy-judge labels risk learning the proxy's bias. Net: the substrate hypothesis under audit is consistent with all evidence — cascade demoted to feature-provider/cold-start, signal in explicit judged edges — and the binding constraint at every recent decision point is the same: ~89 gold labels over 21 topics and no validated judge. The programme keeps re-discovering 'build the judge, grade for topic breadth' and then spending cycles on substrate experiments that refute themselves; the judge harness plan (2026-06-10) is the first attempt aimed squarely at the bottleneck.

levers.name: Domains-interaction aptness geometry (Tourangeau & Sternberg 1981) as a two-feature upgrade to max_hop_cos
levers.what_it_is: Classic empirical finding: metaphor aptness correlates POSITIVELY with between-domain distance (topic-domain vs vehicle-domain far apart) and NEGATIVELY with within-domain distance (the vehicle should occupy in its domain the analogous position the topic occupies in its own), and NOT with overall similarity.
levers.why_relevant: External validation and refinement of the project's verified path-geometry anchor (max_hop_cos 'one big leap', within-topic AUC 0.67/0.85). The literature predicts TWO orthogonal features, not one: (a) leap size across the bridge (already captured by max_hop_cos) and (b) positional/structural congruence within each domain (not yet captured). Implementable as cosine features over existing FastText embeddings + synset domain labels (the SQLUNET `domains` import already planned as type signal). Gives middle-grades writers metaphors that feel daring but coherent — exactly the genre 'gut-punch' target.
levers.accuracy_evidence: Tourangeau & Sternberg: aptness +between-domain distance, -within-domain distance, ~0 overall distance (human-rated). Project-internal concordance: cascade overall-similarity features are at chance for liveness while leap geometry separates — exactly the pattern the 1981 result predicts.
levers.hardware_fit: Trivial: cosine arithmetic over precomputed embeddings, CPU, milliseconds at lookup time. Perfect sovereignty fit (no external calls).
levers.education_fit: Pure geometry over a locally-curated lexicon; zero content-safety or licensing exposure.

levers.name: Career-of-Metaphor + structure-mapping: relational (not attributional) overlap as the aptness feature for NOVEL metaphors
levers.what_it_is: Bowdle & Gentner: novel metaphors are processed as comparisons (analogical structure-mapping); conventional ones as categorisations. SME is the efficient symbolic matcher: prefers shared RELATIONAL structure (predicates over predicates) and ignores attribute matches; no backtracking, polynomial, battle-tested on thousands of cases.
levers.why_relevant: Explains WHY context-free attribute-overlap derivation from the 80k property enrichments was measured dead (AUC 0.55): attributes are the wrong match type for novel-metaphor aptness. The lever is not to run full SME, but to re-shape enrichment toward small predicate structures (relation(topic-part, topic-part)) and score candidate pairs by relational-alignment count — a feature the cascade currently cannot express. Directly targets the product's live (novel) metaphor class rather than the Lakoff dead-metaphor class.
levers.accuracy_evidence: SME robust across thousands of examples over decades; psychological evidence that relational matches drive judged aptness of novel figurative comparisons (structure-mapping corpus of studies). Caveat: no off-the-shelf aptness AUC on a comparable benchmark; this is a theory-grounded feature hypothesis to test against the 89 verdicts.
levers.hardware_fit: Symbolic matching over tiny per-synset predicate sets is CPU-trivial at 1k-100k node scale; representation extraction is the cost (offline LLM batch, see feasibility).
levers.education_fit: Deterministic and inspectable (alignments are explainable to a student: 'X is to its world what Y is to its world'); no licence issues (SME is an algorithm; reimplement).

levers.name: Veale stereotype/category resources as candidate-generation priors (Metaphor Magnet patterns, Thesaurus Rex ad-hoc categories, NOC List)
levers.what_it_is: Veale's line: harvest stereotypical noun properties from web n-gram patterns ('as ADJ as a NOUN'), fine-grained shared ad-hoc categories (Thesaurus Rex), and a hand-curated triple KB of ~1k famous figures (NOC List) explicitly built for metaphor generation. Generation = find vehicles sharing a highly salient stereotype with the topic, then sharpen with affect (+/-).
levers.why_relevant: The methodology (salient-stereotype indexing for vehicle RETRIEVAL, separate from aptness SCORING) maps cleanly onto Metaforge's candidate-generation stage: a stereotype-salience index over the existing property store is a cheap recall booster that the cascade can then rank. Veale's data artefacts also demonstrate the 'small curated KB beats big noisy graph' pattern Metaforge is converging on with graded bridges.
levers.accuracy_evidence: Veale's human evals are small and modest (typical apt/comprehensible ratings ~60-70% in W16-1105-adjacent studies); no held-out AUC tradition. Treat as recall lever, not precision lever.
levers.hardware_fit: Pure lookup tables; trivially CPU/SQLite. But the live afflatus.ucd.ie web services are intermittently defunct and would violate zero-exfiltration anyway — use data/method, never the service.
levers.education_fit: Thesaurus Rex/Metaphor Magnet data is web-harvested (Google n-grams) — needs profanity/stereotype vetting for middle grades; NOC List includes villains/controversial figures, needs curation; NOC is freely available on GitHub for computational-creativity use (verify repo licence file before redistribution in a school product).

levers.name: Conceptual-mapping-conditioned generation + discriminative decoding (Stowe et al. 2021; MERMAID)
levers.what_it_is: Metaphor generation conditioned on explicit source→target conceptual mappings (CM-Gen) and on symbol/commonsense scaffolds with a metaphor-discriminator re-ranking the beam (MERMAID). Both built parallel corpora cheaply via masked-LM literalisation of poetry.
levers.why_relevant: Two transferable mechanics for the Sonnet chain generator and any future local fine-tune: (1) feed the graph's bridge (the explicit topic→vehicle mapping) into the prompt rather than asking for free-form metaphor — the graded metaphor-graph becomes the conditioning input; (2) generate-then-discriminate: over-generate chains, re-rank with the (to-be-built) liveness judge — matching the project's 'loops filter garbage, LLM-graph layer carries positive signal' framing.
levers.accuracy_evidence: MERMAID human eval: best model preferred over 3 baselines 66% of the time; poems enhanced with its metaphors preferred 68%. Pre-LLM-era absolute quality is below Sonnet, but the conditioning/re-ranking ARCHITECTURE is the evidence-backed lever.
levers.hardware_fit: BART-scale (<1B) models fine-tune and run on a single consumer GPU; discriminator is a small classifier. Fully self-hostable.
levers.education_fit: Training data from Gutenberg Poetry corpus (public domain); generated text still needs an output safety filter for a middle-grades product.

levers.name: Small supervised aptness regressors on graded human judgments (Bizzoni & Lappin)
levers.what_it_is: DNN (and by extension any small supervised model) trained on a modest corpus of human metaphor-aptness/paraphrase judgments, predicting binary and gradient aptness.
levers.why_relevant: Existence proof at exactly Metaforge's data scale: useful aptness prediction from hundreds (not tens of thousands) of graded pairs. Endorses the completion-harness plan (pairwise classifier over path-geometry + property features against Julian's verdicts) over representation learning. Their context finding also matters for the grading tool: presenting metaphors IN passage context compresses aptness ratings toward the mean — grade out-of-context for maximal label separation, which the current chain-grading UI already does.
levers.accuracy_evidence: 75% binary accuracy; Pearson .75 / Spearman .68 on gradient aptness from a corpus of ~hundreds of pairs. Context-compression effect replicated in both human and model ratings (1809.01060).
levers.hardware_fit: Logistic/GBM/small-MLP scale; trains in seconds on CPU; inference negligible.
levers.education_fit: Model trained on operator's own verdicts; no external data licence; fully sovereign.

levers.name: Heuristic link prediction on the SUBSTRATE graph (Adamic-Adar/Jaccard/PA + node2vec) as features, sized to 1k-100k nodes
levers.what_it_is: At small scale, classical neighbourhood heuristics are competitive with embeddings WHEN the graph closes triangles; AA drops to AUC 0.5 on triangle-free/lattice structures; GraphSAGE-class only wins on sparser non-clique structure; no method dominates universally. SEAL learns which heuristic fits but needs thousands of edges.
levers.why_relevant: Decision rule for the audit: the graded metaphor edge-set is near-bipartite and non-recurring (5/248 edges recur) → structural heuristics computed ON THE METAPHOR EDGES will be at chance, exactly like AA on triangle-free graphs. But the same heuristics computed on the dense substrate (WordNet/property/ConceptNet layers) — 'number of shared property-neighbours', 'weighted common categories' — are valid cheap FEATURES feeding the pairwise scorer. This cleanly separates where graph-completion machinery can and cannot earn its keep.
levers.accuracy_evidence: Synthetic benchmark (2412.03757): AA ≈ node2vec ≈ GraphSAGE on clique-rich graphs; AA = random (AUC 0.5) with no triangles; 2411.14711 reviews GNN-vs-heuristic parity. node2vec on 100k-node graphs trains in minutes on CPU.
levers.hardware_fit: AA/Jaccard are O(deg²) per pair — microseconds; node2vec/GraphSAGE at 100k nodes: minutes-to-an-hour CPU-only, offline, once. Ideal commodity fit.
levers.education_fit: Pure algorithms over the local DB; zero exfiltration; explainable scores.

levers.name: Domain-level edge generalisation via MetaNet conceptual-metaphor repository (+ Amnestic Forgery RDF)
levers.what_it_is: Hand-curated repository of hundreds of conceptual metaphors as frame-to-frame mappings (source domain → target domain) with FrameNet-style structure; Amnestic Forgery is a machine-readable ontology of it.
levers.why_relevant: Direct attack on the 'synset-level edge recurrence nearly absent' finding: recurrence plausibly exists at DOMAIN level (e.g. EMOTION-IS-WEATHER) even when never repeating at synset level. Lifting graded topic→vehicle edges to domain→domain edges via MetaNet/SQLUNET domain typing gives the completion scorer a level at which 89 verdicts can actually generalise. Second use: MetaNet mappings encode CONVENTIONAL (dead) metaphors — a conventionality prior, i.e. a negative/penalty feature for the live-metaphor product goal, or a 'extend-the-conventional-mapping-novelly' generation strategy.
levers.accuracy_evidence: MetaNet is expert-curated (high precision, ~700 metaphors, incomplete recall); no AUC tradition — value is structural typing, not scoring. Must be validated against the verdicts at domain granularity before trusting.
levers.hardware_fit: Static import into SQLite; negligible compute.
levers.education_fit: Repository is publicly browsable research output (ICSI); Amnestic Forgery ontology published openly (check CC terms on the dataset page before bundling); content is academic and benign, includes some political/moral domains (poverty, gun violence) — filter the seed list for a middle-grades catalogue.

levers.name: ConceptNet 5.5 + Numberbatch as a commonsense bridge layer (HasProperty/CapableOf/UsedFor) with explicit curation pass
levers.what_it_is: CC BY-SA 4.0 multilingual commonsense graph (~1.5M English nodes); relations WordNet lacks (HasProperty, CapableOf, UsedFor, SymbolOf); Numberbatch embeddings (also CC BY-SA) are strong on word relatedness. ATOMIC/IEKG are the event/idiom-flavoured siblings used in figurative-language work.
levers.why_relevant: Fills the relation gap identified by the SME lever: the property enrichments are attribute-heavy, ConceptNet supplies typed relational edges between everyday concepts for free, enabling relational-overlap and substrate-heuristic features (lever 6) without new LLM spend. SymbolOf/HasProperty edges are direct vehicle-retrieval indices for noun-primary metaphor.
levers.accuracy_evidence: Numberbatch led SemEval-2017 relatedness tasks; but OMCS-derived edges are noisy and HasProperty coverage is thin — internally consistent with the refuted context-free derivation: ConceptNet is a recall/feature substrate, not an aptness oracle.
levers.hardware_fit: Full English subgraph fits in SQLite/parquet on a laptop; conceptnet-lite exists; CPU-only queries. Fully offline.
levers.education_fit: Licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 — ShareAlike infects the derived database layer (acceptable for a self-hosted school deployment; constrains any future proprietary DB licensing — flag to operator). Content safety: documented history of offensive crowd-sourced and Wiktionary-derived assertions, partially filtered upstream (blog.conceptnet.io); a school product MUST run its own denylist/curation pass over imported edges.

levers.name: Fine-tuned/calibrated LLM judge for metaphor creativity, bootstrapped from operator verdicts (DiStefano et al. 2024 pattern)
levers.what_it_is: Automatic scoring of metaphor creativity by fine-tuning LLMs on human creativity ratings; reported to correlate strongly with human raters and beat word-count and semantic-distance baselines. Companion findings: Claude-class (Sonnet) judges align best with human creative-quality annotations among tested models; open-judge reliability shows a marked jump at ≥7B.
levers.why_relevant: This is the literature-endorsed path for the project's binding constraint (the UNBUILT live/dead judge): scale Julian's grading by fine-tuning/calibrating a judge on his verdicts, judge offline in batch, and feed accepted edges into the metaphor graph. 89 resolved verdicts are enough for few-shot calibration + a held-out eval set, not yet for fine-tuning — which quantifies the value of continued grading.
levers.accuracy_evidence: DiStefano et al.: fine-tuned-LLM creativity scores correlate strongly with human ratings, outperforming elaboration and semantic-distance baselines (exact r paywalled, 403 on fetch). Persian creativity study (2509.18401): Claude 3.7 Sonnet closest to human annotators on originality/elaboration dimensions; open 7-8B judges usable but degraded on free-form creative judging.
levers.hardware_fit: Judging is OFFLINE batch at HQ: an 8B Q4 judge on an RTX 3060 ≈ 29-42 tok/s ≈ ~3M output tokens/day — thousands of chain judgments/day on one consumer GPU. Nothing runs in schools.
levers.education_fit: No runtime exposure; judge outputs become graph edges shipped as data. Qwen (Apache-2.0) judges avoid Llama-licence output-training restrictions when distilling from verdicts.

levers.name: Aptness-over-conventionality operationalisation (Jones & Estes; Thibodeau & Durgin) for judge criteria and grading rubric
levers.what_it_is: Empirical line showing aptness (how well the vehicle's salient properties characterise the topic) predicts metaphor comprehension/preference better than conventionality or familiarity; processing-fluency accounts of the aptness-conventionality entanglement.
levers.why_relevant: Grounds the product decision already taken (live > dead; Lakoff cohort misaligned) in the psycholinguistic literature, and supplies rubric language for both Julian's grading UI and the judge prompt: rate property-salience fit, not familiarity. Pairs with M02 Ortony salience-imbalance (high-salient in vehicle, low-salient in topic) as the asymmetric property-selection rule.
levers.accuracy_evidence: Jones & Estes 2006: aptness out-predicts conventionality across comprehension measures; replicated/complicated by Thibodeau & Durgin 2011 (fluency confound) — so keep aptness and novelty as separate axes in the verdict model (the two-axis verdict v2 already does this).
levers.education_fit: Improves pedagogical explainability: 'apt because the vehicle's most famous trait fits the topic' is teachable to middle-graders.

levers.name: Confound-controlled judging protocol (anti-surface-feature evaluation design)
levers.what_it_is: 2025 evidence that LLM metaphor 'understanding' is heavily driven by lexical overlap and sentence length rather than metaphorical content; MUNCH shows models struggle specifically on novel+apt metaphors.
levers.why_relevant: Hard constraint on lever 9: an LLM judge scoring Metaforge chains will reward surface artefacts (chain length, word overlap with topic gloss) unless the protocol controls them. Concretely: judge pairwise within-topic with length-matched candidates, strip glosses from the rendering, and audit judge-vs-Julian disagreement specifically on high-lexical-overlap pairs. Also explains why the bad_head 31% contamination matters: mis-extracted heads create surface-overlap artefacts the judge will latch onto.
levers.accuracy_evidence: 2507.15357: across NLI/QA datasets, lexical overlap and sentence length out-influence metaphorical content in LLM performance; MUNCH: paraphrase-judgment failures concentrate on novel-apt items — precisely Metaforge's target class.
levers.education_fit: Indirect: keeps the shipped graph from systematically over-rating glib surface matches that would read as weak metaphors to students.

external.edge_llm_feasibility: Feasible for OFFLINE batch substrate population and judging on one consumer GPU; NOT credible as a runtime aptness judge in schools, and not needed there. Numbers: CPU-only 7-8B Q4 ≈ 8-15 tok/s on typical consumer CPUs (EPYC 7763 ~15 t/s; school desktop class lower) — single-user demo speed, collapses under classroom concurrency; Apple M1 ~30-50 t/s config-dependent; RTX 3060 ≈ 29-42 t/s and RTX 4060 Ti ≈ 38 t/s on Llama-3.1-8B Q4_K_M (localscore.ai, databasemart, geerlingguy Vulkan); RTX 4090 ~180 t/s FP16 7B, more with speculative decoding (sources: github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp discussions #4167/#3847, openbenchmarking.org/test/pts/llama-cpp, mustafa.net/llm-tokens-per-second-benchmarks, localscore.ai/model/1). One RTX-3060-class box at 40 t/s ≈ 3.5M output tokens/day ≈ thousands of chain generations or judgments per day — so the ~$1.9k 10k-topic API generation run has a slower-but-sovereign local fallback measured in days-to-low-weeks, not months. Structured output: llama.cpp GBNF / JSON-schema-to-grammar guarantees syntactic validity of JSON at the sampler level (schema is not seen by the model — must also be described in-prompt; known gaps converting PCRE shorthands, issue #22314; llguidance/outlines/xgrammar are faster, broader-coverage alternatives) — so parse-failure retry storms (as hit in the judge runner) are an avoidable failure mode locally. Licensing for school deployment: Qwen (Apache-2.0) and per 2026 reporting Gemma 4 (Apache-2.0; earlier Gemma releases carried Google's custom terms — verify per-model) are clean; Phi is MIT; Llama's community licence (acceptable-use policy, 700M-MAU cap, and a prohibition on using outputs to improve non-Llama models) is workable for a school but is the most encumbered and the output-training clause complicates distilling judges from Llama outputs. Quality gap, honestly stated: judge reliability shows a marked jump only at ≥7B, and creative/free-form aesthetic judgement is where small open judges degrade most; Sonnet-class models currently align best with human creativity annotations (arxiv 2509.18401), and LLM metaphor competence is substantially surface-feature-driven (arxiv 2507.15357), so an out-of-the-box 1-8B local judge of liveness/aptness should be assumed materially worse than Sonnet until calibrated on operator verdicts — the literature path (DiStefano et al. 2024) is fine-tuning on human ratings, which needs more than the current 89 verdicts (use them as few-shot calibration + held-out eval; fine-tune at ~10^3 verdicts). Recommended architecture under zero-exfiltration: schools run a pure graph/feature lookup (no LLM required at runtime — all heavy lifting is precomputed into the shipped SQLite); optional on-prem 1-4B Q4 CPU model only for surface rendering/paraphrase of already-scored metaphors, never for aptness scoring; generation+judging stay at HQ as batch (API Sonnet preferred for quality, local 8B as sovereign fallback).
dead_ends: Trained KG embeddings (TransE/RotatE/ComplEx/DistMult via PyKEEN-class tooling) on the graded metaphor edge-set: literature shows MRR collapse on sparse triples (≈0.8 → <0.2 at 20% of training triples; false-negative sampling pathology worsens it — arxiv 2209.08769, 2208.07622); at 89 resolved verdicts with 5/248 edge recurrence there is no transductive signal to embed. Revisit only at ~10^3-10^4 graded edges, and even then prefer inductive/feature-based scoring.

SEAL/GNN-style learned link prediction on the metaphor edges: requires thousands of links and recurring local subgraph structure; the metaphor graph is near-bipartite with almost no closed triangles, the regime where neighbourhood-structure methods test at AUC ≈ 0.5 (arxiv 2412.03757, 1802.09691). Structural methods belong on the dense substrate layers, not the verdict layer.

Word-vector parallelogram analogy arithmetic (king-man+woman) as the aptness engine: Linzen 2016 / Rogers et al. 2017 / Peterson et al. show results are heavily nearest-neighbour artefacts and the parallelogram model cannot carry relational reasoning (arxiv 2010.03446; sciencedirect S0010027720302596). Embeddings stay as distance FEATURES, not as an analogy mechanism.

Classical conceptual-blending engines (Divago, COINVENT amalgams): require hand-axiomatised domain microtheories per concept pair; never validated against human aptness judgments at scale; decades of work produced demo-scale outputs (winged-horse class). Not populatable at 20k-word scale on any budget; mine their optimality principles (topology/integration/unpacking) for feature ideas only (tandfonline 09540091.2017.1326463; springer 978-3-319-43610-4_5).

Veale's live web services (Metaphor Magnet/Thesaurus Rex endpoints) as runtime or pipeline dependencies: intermittently defunct, externally hosted (violates zero-exfiltration), and built on Google n-grams snapshots. Use the published method and any redistributable data dumps; never the service.

Off-the-shelf small-LLM 'metaphor understanding' as a quality proxy: 2025 evidence (arxiv 2507.15357) that performance is driven by lexical overlap/sentence length, and MUNCH shows failures concentrate exactly on novel+apt items — the product's target class. Uncalibrated local-LLM liveness scores would systematically reward surface artefacts (and interact badly with the 31% bad_head contamination).

Attribute-overlap aptness scoring generally (the externally-validated version of the internally-refuted context-free derivation): Gentner's relational-vs-attributional results and Tourangeau & Sternberg's null correlation with overall similarity both predict the measured AUC 0.55 — shared-attribute counting cannot be rescued by more enrichment volume; the missing ingredient is relational/positional structure, not more properties.

Runtime LLM inference on school client hardware (Chromebook/old-desktop class): 7-8B Q4 needs ~5-6 GB RAM and yields single-digit tok/s CPU-only; classroom concurrency makes it unusable, and a per-school GPU server contradicts the commodity constraint. Runtime must be precomputed-lookup; this is an architecture decision, not a tuning problem.

Path-geometry-first scorer (generate-then-rank): Sonnet generation as candidate engine, max_hop_cos/std_hop_cos as the ranking features, cascade demoted to gating — builds on the only verified positive signal, conditional on persisting geometry into the schema and surviving the adornment-fragility caveat.

Two-stage calibrated LLM judge (Stage-1 linkage kappa>=0.4 filter, Stage-2 pair liveness kappa>=0.3) as the label-scaling instrument — fully planned (docs/plans/2026-06-10-judge-harness-plan.md), zero code run; the literature path (fine-tune on operator ratings at ~10^3 labels) is the external report's strongest endorsement.

Fix the head extractor at generation time (per-step gloss or sense-index pick inside the chain prompt schema) — prompts report's single highest-signal-per-dollar change; collapses the ~31% bad_head contamination at source and protects both geometry features and verdict transfer.

Relational/structure-mapping features (SME-style predicate alignment; ConceptNet typed relations as free relational substrate) — theory-grounded explanation for why attribute-overlap was measured dead; cheaply testable against the 89 verdicts.

Two-feature aptness geometry (Tourangeau & Sternberg): between-domain leap distance (existing max_hop_cos) + within-domain positional congruence (new) — an upgrade hypothesis to the single-leap feature, implementable on existing embeddings + domain labels.

Conventionality prior as a NEGATIVE feature (MetaNet/Lakoff mapping membership penalises dead metaphors) — aligns the scorer with the live-metaphor genre-writer product goal and reuses the otherwise-misaligned Lakoff assets.

Substrate-layer link-prediction features only (Adamic-Adar/Jaccard/node2vec on the dense property/WordNet/ConceptNet layers, never on the sparse verdict layer) feeding a small supervised pairwise regressor (Bizzoni & Lappin existence proof at ~hundreds of labels) — the external report's decision rule for where graph-completion machinery can earn its keep.
